rule: A local bound directly to a function literal (`const f = () => …`, `local function f`, `let f x = …`, `where f = …`, local `fun`/`def`/`func`, a Rust `fn` item inside a function body, a PHP `$f = function`/`fn`, a C++ `auto f = [..]`, a Kotlin `val f = { }`) is a **named nested function**: ID `outer.f` (Python form), and calls to it are high. Anonymous functions, lambdas, object-literal methods and anonymous-class members fold into the nearest enclosing named function (or the module/type at top level). A caller is never empty.
notes: 'auto sq = [..]' and 'auto add = [&]..' are named nested functions: IDs calc.run.sq / calc.run.add (outer.f), calls to them high (not callback). The anonymous lambda passed to std::for_each folds into calc.run, so its helper(x) call has caller calc.run. std::for_each is a namespace-qualified external function (medium); v is a parameter typed std::vector<int>& → std.vector#begin / #end, medium (external library type, template argument dropped).
